The output frame number and output frame + shutter are converted to input frame numbers and the filter is centered between these two results and the difference between them is the width of the filter.

Setting this to 1 will produce a blend of at least 2 frames. Setting it smaller may produce better filtering and will be faster when the speed is high.
This curve maps the output range to the input range. Steep curve makes it go faster, shallow makes it slower. A downward slope makes it go backwards.

description.plain_text: Retime: Any operators above this are run at a different frame number, or possibly several different frame numbers if filtering is enabled. This can be used to change the timing of the input clip. The checkmarks next to the in/out frame numbers "lock" them to the value you type in. If both output points are locked then the speed is calculated to make the frame ranges match. Otherwise the unlocked ones move to accomodate the speed. The timewarp curve can be used to alter the speed across the frame range. It should pass through 0,0 and 1,1 so that the in and out points work.
description.text:
Retime:

Any operators above this are run at a different frame number, or possibly several different frame numbers if filtering is enabled. This can be used to change the timing of the input clip.

The checkmarks next to the in/out frame numbers "lock" them to the value you type in. If both output points are locked then the speed is calculated to make the frame ranges match. Otherwise the unlocked ones move to accomodate the speed.

The timewarp curve can be used to alter the speed across the frame range. It should pass through 0,0 and 1,1 so that the in and out points work.
